page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb is a dedicated bare-metal server built on the x86_64 architecture, designed for workloads demanding dedicated CPU execution, high memory capacity, and expansive local NVMe storage. The system is driven by an 8-core, 16-thread Intel Xeon 2288G processor operating at a 3.7 GHz base clock speed, backed by 16 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 128 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation, alongside a single bundled 3,840 GB NVMe SSD for high-capacity local storage. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, and the host operates without hypervisor overhead or GPU hardware acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong performance in memory and single-threaded operations. The server attained a top-tier PassMark memory benchmark score of 3,594.89 and demonstrated strong single-core data processing in gzip compression (36.22 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.23 GB/sec). Standard compute metrics—such as stress-ng CPU tests and Geekbench scores—consistently placed within the median range. Conversely, large-block uncached memory read (29.76 GB/sec) and write (15.32 GB/sec) bandwidth test in the lower quartile, reflecting the constraints of the processor's memory bus. Similarly, absent dedicated tensor acceleration, inference speeds for medium-sized LLM models remain low.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal profile provides substantial resource density by packaging dedicated 8-core execution, 128 GB of RAM, and multi-terabyte NVMe storage without virtualization penalties. This configuration makes it an effective deployment target for standalone relational databases, Redis caching layers, web serving architectures, software build runners, and persistent file processing pipelines.

The vbm-8c-132gb serves applications requiring predictable performance and large working sets, while workloads reliant on advanced matrix math, AVX-512 extensions, or massive parallel thread counts will find better alignment in higher-tier multi-socket or GPU-accelerated server families.
description: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb is a dedicated bare-metal server engineered for memory-dense and storage-intensive applications. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 2288G processor operating at 3.7 GHz, the platform provides 8 physical cores and 16 hardware threads with no virtualization layer. Hardware resources include 128 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-thread ratio, alongside a bundled 3,840 GB NVMe SSD array. In benchmark testing, the platform exhibits top-tier PassMark memory performance and strong single-threaded data compression throughput, while large-block uncached memory bandwidth registers lower against modern multi-channel server platforms. The lack of accelerator hardware restricts suitability for complex machine learning tasks, as demonstrated by weak medium-model inference speeds. This bare-metal configuration offers strong resource density and fixed predictability for database hosting, in-memory caches, static content distribution, and persistent transaction-oriented workloads requiring high I/O throughput.
